message:
The fingertip holds together because soft skin pressure reaches both sensing films on flat facets and both signal paths join in one safe message. Plain words first: the thin stack, flat tiles and dual paths match in place and in time. The stack stays under 2.50 mm in the GelSight High-Resolution Robot Tactile Sensors (E2) over the faceted drape sketch (E65) with 3.18 mm flex bend in the BioTac Product Manual (E43), static force goes through the 9.00 ms update in the AD7147A Rev B (E41) where CDC means Capacitance-to-Digital Converter, and fast shake goes direct to the 1 Msps converter in the STM32 notes (E68) where ADC means Analog-to-Digital Converter and MCU means Microcontroller Unit, joined by heartbeat plus interrupt in the What is a Track Circuit (E74) with two-channel wiring in the How to wire e-stop (E76) where SPI means Serial Peripheral Interface.

Light touch and full grip fit finger scale on everyday checks with one unit slip reconciled. Plain words first: a grain-of-sand touch still clears the chip and a milk-bottle pinch does not bottom out on spoon-light power. The numbers that decide it are 0.470 mm spot at 5.78 kPa in the Hertz contact radius (E14) on 0.269 pF base in the base capacitance gap (E26) giving 3.57 fF change in the check deltaC (E55) which corrects 0.00357 fF in the delta capacitance calculation (E28) as a thousand-fold unit slip, giving 14.6 steps where LSB means Least Significant Bit in the signal margin counts (E62), spanning to 213 kPa at 50 N in the dual-range sweep (E64) with 125 kPa hold in the pressure at hold (E93) from 9.81 N per finger in the required normal calculation (E85), in 20.0 mm by 22.0 mm size inside 18.0 mm by 28.0 mm finger in the Free and Forced Vibration Modes (E60), at 14.0 g mass in the mass budget sum (E53) about one-and-half teaspoons, 0.0991 W power in the power budget sum (E51) about one-tenth of a small lamp, 51.2 kbit per s rate in the SPI rate (E52), and 30.0 ms window inside 43.2 ms gap in the slip gap calculation (E84) from 53.6 ms to 96.8 ms in the stick-to-slip simulation (E38) needing 96.8 thousand accumulations per s where MAC means multiply-accumulate in the FIR rate (E78) where FIR means Finite Impulse Response.

No blocking objection is open and every ready vote on this version is answered, leaving only hardware proof as named bench tests. Plain words first: timing, margin, fit and fail-safe survive strongest objections and shake and rub need built hardware to prove. Zero blocking objections stand on the board, so Dr. Amara Okafor is answered by 26.8 N tear in the tear force calculation (E92) against 9.81 N hold with 0.880 grip in the silicone grip liner (E88), Prof. Kenji Tanaka is answered by 14.6 steps margin with no saturation, Dr. Elena Vasquez is answered by 2200 Hz direct PVDF path where PVDF means Polyvinylidene Fluoride vibration film inside the 43.2 ms gap, and Dr. Marcus Reid is answered by dorsal routing clear of rim slip in the Dynamics of fingertip slip (E67) plus fail-safe interrupt, with rub-cycle tear, shake-plus-pull continuity and timed 30 ms loop as bench tests.

RECORD: Decided F1 molded Shore A 10 dome plus ridges plus sipes, F2 nail-backed faceted core with M2 plus dovetail, F3 capacitive plus PVDF, F4 2.00 mm pitch centroid to 1 mm, F5 100 to 500 Hz power plus shear check in 30 ms, F6 fail-safe heartbeat plus interrupt plus SPI; numbers that stand are 0.470 mm at 5.78 kPa (E14), 0.269 pF base (E26), 3.57 fF change (E55 corrects E28), 14.6 LSB (E62), to 213 kPa (E64) with 125 kPa hold (E93) from 9.81 N (E85), 43.2 ms gap (E84) with 30 ms window (E38), 14.0 g (E53), 0.0991 W (E51), 51.2 kbit per s (E52), 20.0 by 22.0 mm (E43 E60); still open are only named bench tests owed as hardware proof, no blocking objection open, all four members voted ready on v1 and answered. My position: ready, because the concept works physically, fits finger scale on everyday checks, and builds from purchasable parts with only timed hardware proof left as bench tests.
Note on Dr. Amara Okafor: proved rim shear and tear margin with thin stack that keeps light touch alive.
Note on Prof. Kenji Tanaka: proved 14.6 step margin without saturation and faceted drape that keeps tiles flat.
Note on Dr. Elena Vasquez: proved 30 ms dual-path timing inside slip gap with direction from rim shear.
Note on Dr. Marcus Reid: proved mount fit, dorsal routing and fail-safe message with trivial compute load.
